newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium slumps to 2-1/4 year low as metals close weakly.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium slumps to 2-1/4 year low as metals close weakly.

text.p: Aluminium carved out a fresh 2-1/4 year low and copper failed to hold above the $1,900 level as the London Metal Exchange (LME) closed weakly and traders forecast more losses to come.
"The close on copper certainly is not very encouraging," one trader said.
The metals suffered the heaviest losses but it was a generally bleak day across the commodity markets.
Three months aluminium dived to a fresh 2-1/4 year low of $1,340 early on the LME but clawed its way up to close at $1,352, a $25 loss from Wednesday, on trade buying, mostly from the Far East.
"I'm not convinced it's enough to keep it up," a trader said referring to the buying which the low price attracted.
Fresh buying was unlikely to be encouraged above $1,330, the lows of early June 1994, then the psychological $1,300 region, market analysts said.
Gold also closed lower slipping to $379.35 an ounce compared with $380.60 on Wednesday.
Dealers said the gold price could take a fresh shot at getting over $380 but that would not necessarily change the market's overriding bearish trend.
"It is not finished with the $380 yet, but if the resistance (selling) is still in there at $380-$381.50, we may see gold moving lower," one dealer said.
London cocoa futures prices closed lower marking Thursday's close as its fourth consecutive losing day as selling continued against dwindling demand.
Origin selling was cited from Nigeria, Ivory Coast and Indonesia, while investment funds and trade houses also divested themselves of cocoa holdings.
The benchmark March contract ended seven stg lower on the day at 985 stg a tonne, just off its session low of 983 stg.
White sugar futures lost earlier gains in mostly routine business before turning positive again in late afternoon.

The positive physical undertone helped sustain prices with Syria buying 26,000 tonnes of sugar for November shipment but it was less clear whether or not Sri Lanka had settled on accepting a tender for 12,5000 tonnes.
Traders in Colombo said suppliers had been asked to resubmit bids before Friday but London traders thought the tender had been filled.
Robusta coffee futures could not recoup early losses by the close as aggressive origin hedge selling met very little roaster buying interest.
The front-month November contract was $17 down on the day to close at $1,495 a tonne.
The U.S. grain markets were quiet and mixed with corn weaker and soybeans holding Wednesday's gains achieved on adverse weather forecasts.
